articles.title: Big briefs for men are back – and I couldn’t be happier | Adrian Chiles
articles.summary: Jude Bellingham’s new Calvin Klein ad campaign is heartening in so many ways, but the first thing I noticed was the capacious underpants. I have surprisingly strong feelings about underpants, or rather the celebrities who endorse them.
body: While I cannot imagine ever buying Calvin Klein pants, I do take an interest in their models. I could have sworn blind David Beckham was one of them, but it turns out otherwise. Armani, H&M and Hugo Boss, but not Calvin Klein. Freddie Ljungberg was a CK man. Smouldering away, but a bit too much body oil for my taste. Looked a right slippery fish. The biggest letdown was Jeremy Allen White, the actor from The Bear. I took him for someone a bit like me – ate too much and therefore on the paunchy side. Suddenly, he was up on billboards in his undies, all toned and muscly, with abs as clanking hard as his cast-iron pans. Disappointing. What a sellout.

articles.title: You will die. That’s why your life is worth living
articles.summary: What does the tech elite offer? The immortality grift. But there’s another way to look at our previous time on Earth. Ted “the Kid” Williams was perhaps one of the greatest hitters baseball has ever seen. He played for the Boston Red Sox for nearly 20 years.
body: His two younger children had his body carted off by private jet to Alcor Life Extension Foundation, a cryonics facility in Scottsdale, Arizona. There, his head was severed from his body in a process called neuroseparation, thought to increase the quick-freeze preservation of the brain. His head and body were placed in stainless steel nitrogen tanks.
He is still there, alongside his son John Henry, who died two years later – two of the 263 people the company claims to be preserving for future revival.

Williams’s oldest daughter, who wanted him cremated, challenged her siblings’ claim that their father chose this frosty, inanimate suspension. She ultimately dropped the lawsuit. What the baseball legend got, like it or not, was eternity in a tin can.
Twenty-four years after his death, the promise of immortality is mogging our culture, having shifted from cryotanks to the thriving wellness marketplace.
points: But there’s another way to look at our previous time on Earth.

articles.title: A local’s guide to Belgrade: the best sights, restaurants and nightlife in a city in flux
articles.summary: A new optimism pervades the Serbian capital following the recent elections, making it a great time to visit its bars, clubs, markets and riverside hotspots. There’s a celebratory mood in Belgrade, the Serbian capital.
body: Demonstrations grew into a nationwide challenge to the government and finally, last month the student-backed list won an outright majority in parliamentary elections – a dramatic shift in Serbia’s political landscape. Crowds gathered in Slavija Square, and celebrations spilled into the streets and bars. The formation of a new government still lies ahead, but the city feels full of possibility.

One of Europe’s oldest cities, Belgrade sits at the confluence of the Sava and Danube rivers. With a large student population and a thriving creative scene, it has informal, sociable energy: cafe terraces fill during the day, while DJ bars and clubs keep the city moving late into the night. Historic streets, neoclassical and art nouveau buildings sit alongside modernist architecture, former industrial spaces and new waterfront developments. As founder of Still in Belgrade I’ve spent more than a decade exploring the city’s art, culture and music scene – here are some of my favourite things to do.

articles.title: Rachel Roddy’s recipe for Neapolitan mostaccioli, or spiced biscuits dipped in chocolate | A kitchen in Rome
articles.summary: Halfway between a cake and a biscuit, with a throat-warming level of spice, these Italian treats have been around since medieval times, and only get better with age. Established in 1982 by sisters Piera, Pina and Grazia Saverese, Pasticceria Savarese is a Neapolitan pastry shop in south-east Rome.
body: The house speciality is la pastiera Napoletana, a latticed tart with a deep filling of ricotta, wheat berries, sugar, milk, candied fruit and spices – it’s traditional at Easter, but available here all year round. La pastiera was the reason we first visited the shop a few years ago, on the recommendation of a Neapolitan friend who dislikes cooking as much as she likes eating. She also recommended the diamond- or rombo -shaped mostaccioli, which are halfway between a cake and a biscuit and spiced in a way that warms the throat (they remind me of Yorkshire parkin biscuits); they are also completely covered in dark chocolate.

articles.title: 24 Black Wedding Dresses for the Non-Traditional Bride
articles.summary: Does your bridal style lean non-traditional? Choose a black wedding dress for your big day; here, great designs from the likes of Vivienne Westwood, Tory Burch, and more.
body: If you’ve never pictured yourself walking down the aisle in a white gown, consider this your sign to go with your gut. Black wedding dresses are a striking alternative for brides who want something unexpected and aren’t afraid to break with tradition. Opting for a darker palette is hardly a new idea, either: Sarah Jessica Parker famously wore a black Morgane Le Fay design for her 1997 nuptials, and Chloë Sevigny chose an all-black look for her 2020 city hall ceremony. More recently, Emma Roberts tapped Monique Lhuillier to design a black look for her after-party ensemble—proof that you can buck convention at any stage of your big day.

Moody as it may seem, a black wedding dress is also seasonless; the trick is finding one in a fabric that feels right for the setting and time of year. Thicker materials like velvet and heavy crepe are perfect for fall and winter fêtes, while silk and airy organza add a lighter touch for warm-weather celebrations (a breezy black mini on the beach is not taboo!). A two-tone design—say, a gown with an ivory bodice and inky skirt—offers the best of both worlds if you’re not quite ready to fully part with white.

articles.title: Creative Director Luca Marchetto on Redesign Atelier Menabóh: “It’s Like Therapy”
articles.summary: The redesign atelier soft-launched in Tuscany last week, under the creative direction of Jordanluca co-founder Luca Marchetto. Vogue Business got an exclusive first look.
body: Most upcycling services shout about their sustainability credentials, but Italian startup Menabóh is flipping the script. “Upcycling is too connected to patchwork and the DIY aesthetic,” says co-founder Gaia Rialti. “We could use ‘transforming’ or ‘reimagining’, but I think ‘redesign’ explains exactly what we do: it’s upcycling with an added layer of creative direction. It’s bespoke and made-to-measure; it’s a new kind of luxury.”

Gone are the mystery boxes Menabóh started out with back in 2021, which peddled upcycled fashion alongside vintage pieces and unsold garments from other brands. The same goes for its second guise, an online marketplace used to connect customers with upcyclists across Italy, which left Menabóh with a disjointed tangle of upcycling projects it had little control over, and limited potential for brand recognition.
points: The redesign atelier soft-launched in Tuscany last week, under the creative direction of Jordanluca co-founder Luca Marchetto.

articles.title: Inside The Or Foundation’s Plans to Overhaul Kantamanto Market
articles.summary: Ghana’s Kantamanto Market is one of the world’s largest circular fashion ecosystems, but poor sanitation, fire risks and flooding are a constant threat to its survival. Could a new design help it last?
body: In January 2025, a devastating fire broke out at Ghana’s Kantamanto Market, burning around 60% of the market to ashes and wiping out thousands of livelihoods in the process. It wasn’t the first fire at Kantamanto Market, and it might not be the last.

“For many customers, the market is not a safe or attractive place to shop,” says Branson Skinner, co-founder and executive producer of The Or Foundation, a US-Ghanaian non-profit that operates in and around Kantamanto Market. “We have made some progress — at least five fires have been stopped thanks to the unified security force and fire extinguishers integrated across the market — but until the underlying issues of fire lanes, up-to-code electricity, fire-resistant building materials and water access are addressed, the market remains vulnerable.”

articles.summary: From archival Hermès to matching reindeer pajamas, longtime friends Kim Kardashian and Jennifer Lawrence took girls’ night dressing to its coziest conclusion.
body: Kim Kardashian and Jennifer Lawrence might occupy opposite ends of the celebrity style spectrum, but it turns out they have more in common than a shared appreciation for archival fashion and an Hermès handbag. That is, a penchant for a good old-fashioned slumber party.

But the evening’s most unexpected fashion moment was still to come. Later, the pair were photographed at the Four Seasons hotel having traded their going-out clothes for matching chocolate-brown velour Skims dressing gowns, festive reindeer-print pajamas, and oversized sunglasses. A slumber party? Some conveniently timed holiday content? Why not both? Between two actors, mothers, and business founders, there was surely plenty to catch up on.

articles.title: Spinach Artichoke Baked Potatoes
articles.summary: The iconic dip becomes a cheesy stuffing for these crispy skinned potatoes.
body: This baked potato stuffed with spinach-artichoke dip is the ultimate solo comfort meal. Classic twice-baked potatoes require two trips to the oven to deliver a pillowy, gussied-up filling and crispy skins all in one bite. Here, I’ve streamlined the workflow with a microwave. By zapping your spuds to start, you can reduce the overall baking time without sacrificing texture. Pick a large russet (or Idaho) for the best results; their relatively high starch and low moisture content helps them bake up airy and light, not gummy.

The rich, velvety filling that melts over top comes together in moments while your spud cooks. Cream cheese and mozzarella pack in enough dairy richness for a satisfying cheese pull and mellow out the subtle bitterness of baby spinach and nutty tang of artichoke hearts. (It’s important that your cream cheese is room temperature before you mash it in with the veggies. If it’s still got a chill from the fridge, it won’t fully incorporate.) The Worcestershire sauce is optional, but just a few shakes from the bottle bring instant savory depth to the filling.
points: The iconic dip becomes a cheesy stuffing for these crispy skinned potatoes.
